stemBlocks.value: The vectors u and v are parallel and point in the same direction, where u has components k and 6, and v has components 4 and 3. (a) Determine the value of k. (b) Calculate |u|. (c) Write u as a scalar multiple of v.
Think first: Parallel vectors are scalar multiples of each other, so the same multiplier must apply to both rows.

strategyBlocks.value: Compare the components you know to find the scalar, use it to find k, then apply Pythagoras for the magnitude.

whyThisWorks.value: Two vectors are parallel exactly when one is a scalar multiple of the other, so a single number rescales both components together. The scalar is positive here, which is what keeps the directions the same — a negative scalar would have made them point opposite ways. The magnitudes scale by the same factor: |v| = 5 and |u| = 10.
